newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia aims for five pct GDP growth rate.
newsitem.headline: Namibia aims for five pct GDP growth rate.

text.p: Namibia plans to achieve a five percent annual growth rate and reduce its budget deficit to three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by the turn of the century, President Sam Nujoma said on Tuesday.

Opening a regional conference on poverty eradication in Southern Africa, he said the First National Development Plan, implemented in 1995, "seeks to revive and sustain economic growth...(to) achieve an annual five percent average growth rate in real gross domestic product between 1995 and the year 2000."
He added that the plan was also designed to "increase real gross national income per capita by 12 percent."

Also envisaged under the plan is the creation of 70,000 jobs in the formal and 40,000 in the informal sector. Unemployment and underemployment are estimated to account for 60 percent, or 263,000 out of some 435,000 employable adults.

The 13 percent of households identified in 1994 as severely poor will be cut to seven percent; poor households cut to 40 percent from 47; and below-average income households to 50 percent from 60 by the turn of the century.
The most effective way of achieving this goal was through education, Nujoma emphasised.
"An educated populace will never be threatened by poverty," he said. "Hence it is vital that education becomes a central pillar in our efforts (to fight poverty)."
Equally important, were the amicable and equitable sharing of national resources, especially land, and the forming of international partnerships.
According to United Nations projections, Sub-Saharan Africa is the only major region in the world where poverty is expected to increase into the 21st century.
The four-day conference representatives from Namibia, Botswana, Zambia, Malawi and Angola plan to formulate a common regional strategy to minimise the effects of poverty in Southern Africa.
